_about: The narration of Scenario 2's narrated cut, draft 2 (S317 SkyCompass, 2026-10-02), voiced by Sierra. Sam, 2026-10-02: "write a script for the scenario 2 video for an ElevenLabs narrator. Keep it very simple and focused and see if you can select a female voice model to narrate and give her the name Sierra on the video as a sample", and "The music can drop to background level." One or two plain sentences per scene of the current Scenario 2 picture (the introduction's v7: the average allocation, the targets slide, December 30, 2026, the CPL funding page), about 330 words where draft 1 had 430. Every figure is the film's, read from the engine under the live config, md5 764fd264 (checked live 2026-10-02): $35,000,000; about $25 million to 118 institutions; the $150,000 to $400,000 range and the $213,901 average; 4,366.7 FTES statewide for each priority; 34.5 FTES for the average Access target. The voice says the figures in words and writes MAP as map, so the captions and the aligner read what she says.

engine.name: elevenlabs
engine._why: Bella is an ElevenLabs premade voice (always available, unlike a library voice, which its owner can withdraw): "warm, bright, and professional... Standard American accent... crisp diction and a deliberate, rhythmic pace". Sierra is the name the film gives her (Sam, 2026-10-02). One generation per scene through the ElevenLabs connector; each scene's `read` names its clip and generation, and `text_sha1` is the SHA-1 of the text it was read from. narrate.py brings every clip to one speech level, -20 dBFS RMS, 2 dB over the Kokoro read it replaces, so the score sits further back.

layout._why: The narrated cut paces each scene as its lead-in (the seam, its barrier and the first reveal), its clip, and its air; Sam, 2026-09-26: "slow down and lengthen the timing a bit to accommodate readability and narration."

scenes.text: Hi, I'm Sierra. Here's how CPL Initiative funding works for your college.

cues.why: the name beneath the lockup, Narrated by Sierra
the title, CPL Initiative Funding: How It Works, letter by letter
the kicker, An introduction for colleges

scenes.text: The state set aside thirty-five million dollars in one-time funding. About twenty-five million goes directly to one hundred eighteen institutions. The rest funds statewide CPL projects, technology, and two Chancellor's Office positions that support colleges.

cues.why: the kicker, One-time funding for 2026–27
cues.skip: the picture shows it before the $35,000,000 counter, and the voice names it after; the counter takes the cue

cues.why: the line, set aside by the state to help colleges build credit for prior learning
cues.skip: the voice says it about a second before the counter lands, and the picture needs 2.2 seconds of film before it; pinned, it would hurry the count, so the counter takes the cue and the line follows its words

the bar's first segment and its label, $25,240,308 directly to 118 institutions
the second segment and its label, $9,759,692 for statewide CPL projects and technology and two Chancellor’s Office positions

scenes.text: Each institution has a maximum allocation for the two years, from one hundred fifty thousand to four hundred thousand dollars. The average is about two hundred fourteen thousand.
scenes.air_why: The picture runs six seconds past the average marker (its bottom line, Smaller institutions are brought up to the base. The largest are held at the cap.), and the voice ends two seconds after naming the average; with the usual 0.8 s of air the marker and the cap led their words by 2.6 and 2.2 s.

scenes.text: Each allocation splits into a credit share and a noncredit share. Only noncredit outcomes count toward the noncredit share.

cues.why: the heading, The average splits in two

scenes.text: Two priorities carry the funding, in equal shares. Access counts applied CPL units. Completion counts transcribed CPL units, with the map counselor step checked. The Chancellor's Office reports on career attainment together with the innovation projects.

cues.why: the heading, Two priorities carry the funding

scenes.text: The model sets each priority's statewide target from its funding and the FTES reimbursement rate: about four thousand three hundred sixty-seven FTES for each.

scenes.text: Your college has its own target under each priority. Thirty semester units of CPL make one FTES. For the average allocation, the Access target is about thirty-four and a half FTES. Reach half the target, and your college qualifies for half the share. The full target qualifies for the full share, and that share is the ceiling.

the bar fills to half its target

scenes.text: Before the Chancellor's Office releases any funding, your college meets three minimum conditions by December thirtieth: name a CPL coordinator, put your local confirmation of participation on file, and upload Joint Services Transcripts for at least seventy-five percent of enrolled veterans. Until then, the funding your college demonstrates is held in reserve for it.
